description: Signals keep trains from hitting each other.

pages.title: Signals and Schedules
pages.text: Signals keep trains from hitting each other. A Train Signal splits the track into segments, and each segment holds one train at a time. Signals only govern trains that nobody is driving.

pages.title: Train Signal
pages.text: Placed beside a track like a station. A scheduled train never crosses one against its direction unless a second signal faces that way.

pages.title: Two modes
pages.text: A wrench switches a signal to its second mode. A brass-mode signal is meant to lead into ordinary ones: it holds a train back if, once inside, it could not leave the next segment at once. That keeps queued trains out of a busy junction.

pages.title: Redstone
pages.text: A redstone signal forces a Train Signal red, and a red signal gives a comparator output. Nixie Tubes attached to a signal make the lights easier to read from a distance.

pages.title: Train Observer
pages.text: Select a track, place the observer nearby. It fires when a train crosses the marker and can be filtered by cargo.

pages.title: Schedules
pages.text: A **Train Schedule** holds a list of stops and the conditions to leave each. Right-click it to edit, then give it to a driver. Any mob, or a Blaze Burner, seated in front of Train Controls counts as a conductor. You can take the schedule back at any time.

pages.title: Train Schedule
pages.text: Stations are the stops. Conditions can be a delay, a cargo level, a redstone signal and more.

pages.title: Going further
pages.text: Steam 'n' Rails adds track switches and semaphores, and Railways Navigator adds route planning and penalty anchors that make trains avoid stretches of track. See [#](2E5AAC)[Train Add-ons](entry://transport/train_addons)[#]().
